title: Do not let the mouth become a dumping ground
summary: This meets speech already fouled by greed, slander, anger, and self-praise. The line insists that only words bringing honor are worth keeping.
takeaway: Speak only what can bear honor.
lifeApplication: Before the sharp comment or clever put-down, feel the tongue against the teeth. If the words dirty the mouth, do not give them voice.

source.shortMeaning: Speech that carries greed and slander degrades the mouth; honorable words preserve it.
source.lifeApplication: When harsh words rise, stop at the mouth and ask whether they can survive God's door.

evidence.coreClaim: Speech that carries greed and slander degrades the mouth; honorable words preserve it.
evidence.turn: Keep only the speech that can stand at God's Door.
evidence.practicalImplication: Before the sharp comment or clever put-down, feel the tongue against the teeth. If the words dirty the mouth, do not give them voice.
